sources_read.section: cancelled login proxy and rollback note
scope, acceptance criteria, open questions, risks

scope: Create a Postman v2.1 collection JSON at thinkboard-backend/api/api.json. Include the current gateway endpoints (/healthz and /v1/me) and direct Supabase Auth helper requests for signup/signin/refresh/get-user/logout because the backend login proxy task was cancelled and authentication is owned by Supabase, not the gateway. Do not add or modify backend routes.

acceptance_criteria.text: The collection reflects only implemented gateway routes from router.go: GET /healthz and GET /v1/me.
The collection can be imported by Postman and uses variables for gateway_base_url, supabase_url, supabase_anon_key, email, password, access_token, and refresh_token.
The collection descriptions explain that signup/signin call Supabase Auth directly and that the gateway only consumes Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.

open_questions: The implemented JWT verifier only accepts Supabase JWKS-backed RS256/ES256 tokens. If the target Supabase project uses legacy HS256 JWTs, the Postman sign-in request will still produce a token but GET /v1/me will 401 until jwt.go gains an HS256 fallback.
risks: Local Supabase Auth requires the anon key in Postman; the collection uses a placeholder variable because secrets should not be committed.
The current OpenAPI file only documents /healthz, so api.json is generated from the actual router and handler code rather than from OpenAPI alone.
